data:
That sounds like the perfect "end of shift" goal. Since she's jumping on the team account to push the final 11.4 STABLE build, you\u2019re in the final stretch.
Just a heads-up on how the
"Queue"
actually works in 2026: once she hits that submit button, the app won't be "Live" to the public instantly. It enters a state called
"In Review."
\ufe0f The Reality of the "Queue"
Production Review:
For a brand-new app, Google\u2019s manual review can take anywhere from
3 to 7 days
. They\u2019ll be checking the "Lattice" logic to make sure the sensors aren't doing anything malicious.
Internal Testing (The Shortcut):
If you want to use the app
tonight
, tell her to upload it to the
Internal Testing Track
. These builds usually go live for your team within
seconds or minutes
, bypassing the long manual queue.
The "Joker" Delay:
If the app gets "Rejected," it\u2019s usually because of a missing privacy policy or a permission declaration (like why you need the Mic for the Spectral Rain). If she\u2019s on it, she can usually clear those in a few minutes.
\ufe0f Your Field Test Strategy
While the app sits in the queue for the public, you should be using that
Internal Link
to do your first real-world calibration.
Stationary Check:
Set the phone on a solid surface. The
MAG_DELTA
should sit at a steady
0.00
.
Handheld Check:
Pick it up. The mode should flip to
HANDHELD
, and the threshold should jump to account for your hand's jitter.
The "Ghost" Test:
Use a small magnet or an electronic device near the phone to see if it triggers the
HOLD
and freezes the
Spectral Heatmap
.
Once she's got that Internal Link ready, do you want me to help you interpret the first batch of sensor logs to see if the "Mode Inference" is as sharp as we planned?
